label: FICTIONAL DATA / SANDBOX
disclaimer: Every league, team, player, analyst, statistic and report in this corpus is invented for the Ask Pivot research sandbox. None of it describes a real NBA player, team, contract or game. It must never be mixed with Pivot's NBA data.

league.name: Pivot Synthetic League
league.season_note: A fictional season label. The statistics are invented for evaluation and teaching.

teams.name: Hartford Comets
teams.identity: Contender built on five-out spacing around a franchise lead guard; lost its last playoff series when opposing guards repeatedly got downhill.
default_constraints: Closing lineups need four credible shooters around the center (coaching staff, S21).
Timeline is this season's playoffs, not a multi-year build.

teams.name: Omaha Riverhawks
teams.identity: Rebuilding club prioritising players 24 or younger with development upside, and looking for a young lead creator.
default_constraints: Prefer players aged 24 or younger (front office, S23).
Willing to move veterans whose timeline does not match the rebuild.

teams.name: Albuquerque Sundogs
teams.identity: Defense-first playoff hopeful whose half-court offense stalls; needs shooting volume and secondary creation and will accept some defensive drop-off.
default_constraints: Keep the team-defense identity intact (front office, S24).
Open to discussing Bastian Holloway if it returns shooting (S24).

teams.name: Savannah Tides
teams.identity: Pace-and-space small-ball team that is getting beaten on the glass and at the rim; wants size without slowing down.
default_constraints: Do not slow the pace identity (front office, S25).
A non-shooting center is acceptable only if he protects the rim (S25).

priority_dimensions.label: Point-of-attack defense
priority_dimensions.description: Containing the ball handler at the start of a possession: staying in front, navigating screens, pressuring without fouling.

priority_dimensions.label: Wing / positional defense
priority_dimensions.description: Guarding bigger wings one-on-one and switching across positions.

priority_dimensions.label: Team / help defense
priority_dimensions.description: Rotations, help timing and communication — defending as part of five.

priority_dimensions.label: Spacing
priority_dimensions.description: Whether defenders must stay attached: shooting volume, willingness and gravity, not three-point percentage alone.

priority_dimensions.label: Secondary creation
priority_dimensions.description: Second-side playmaking, attacking closeouts and keeping the ball moving when the primary creator is denied.

priority_dimensions.label: Primary creation
priority_dimensions.description: Running the offense: pick-and-roll reads, collapsing the defense, creating for others.

priority_dimensions.label: Rim protection
priority_dimensions.description: Deterring and contesting shots at the basket.

priority_dimensions.label: Rebounding
priority_dimensions.description: Finishing possessions on the defensive glass and creating extra ones on offense.

priority_dimensions.label: Youth / development upside
priority_dimensions.description: Age and the room a player has left to improve.

priority_dimensions.label: Availability
priority_dimensions.description: Games played and durability across the season.

players.name: Niko Reed
players.summary: Elite on-ball and wing defender; low-volume shooter whom playoff defenses left open.

players.name: Theo Vance
players.summary: High-volume, accurate movement shooter; defensive reports on him conflict and there is no playoff sample.

players.name: Bastian Holloway
players.summary: The best point-of-attack defender in the sample; a non-shooter whose lineups lose spacing.

players.name: Ilan Marchetti
players.summary: Strong secondary playmaker and good shooter; struggles to contain at the point of attack.

players.name: Mateo Cruz
players.summary: Young pick-and-roll creator; small and a weak on-ball defender; free-throw data is missing.

players.name: Dante Cruz
players.summary: Rim protector and rebounder who does not shoot from three.

players.name: Wes Calder
players.summary: Once graded an elite wing defender (2023); a 2026 re-evaluation finds clear on-ball decline but good shooting.

players.name: Dorian Pike
players.summary: High-usage scorer with a high three-point percentage on very low volume and poor defense; subject of a promotional agent memo.

players.name: Amari Fenwick
players.summary: Twenty-year-old long wing with defensive tools and an unfinished jump shot.

players.name: Rafael Sorensen
players.summary: Floor-spacing big who is a weak rim protector; already on the Comets.

players.name: Lucas Achterberg
players.summary: Young seven-footer who dominates the glass in drop coverage and is slow-footed in space.

players.name: Niko Valdez
players.summary: Steady backup point guard on the Comets; limited minutes and availability.

unavailable_facts.reason: No source in this corpus records Mateo Cruz's free-throw percentage; the guard profile (S02) marks it as not recorded.
Dante Cruz attempted 0.1 threes per game (seven all season); the frontcourt profile (S19) withholds a percentage on that sample.
Lucas Achterberg attempted no threes this season, so there is no three-point percentage (S19).

conflicts.summary: Theo Vance's point-of-attack defense is graded B in a January 2026 report (S05) but C+ in a November 2025 report (S06).
conflicts.guidance: S05 is more recent and covers a larger sample; S06's screen-navigation concern is specific. Neither covers playoff possessions, so the question is open for a playoff role.

conflicts.summary: Wes Calder was graded an A- wing defender in December 2023 (S11) and C+ in February 2026 (S12).
conflicts.guidance: S11 is more than two years older and predates his age-related decline; prefer S12 for a current evaluation while noting the history.

conflicts.summary: The Comets front office (S20) blames the playoff exit on point-of-attack defense; an analytics note (S22) argues defensive rebounding and transition defense mattered more.
conflicts.guidance: Both diagnoses can be partly true. This is a judgment for the GM, not something the documents settle.

conflicts.summary: An agent memo (S29, untrusted) calls Dorian Pike an elite shooter; the analytics note (S14) shows his 41.2% comes on 1.1 attempts per game and does not create spacing.
conflicts.guidance: S29 is promotional third-party material. S14 explains the volume context.
